raw.transcript: First, power off your modem and router completely, then unplug them for about 20 seconds to clear any stuck state. Next, plug the modem back in, wait until all its lights look stable, then turn the router back on. After that, on your phone or computer, forget the Wi-Fi network and rejoin it by typing the password fresh. If it still drops, move closer to the router and try a different device to see if the issue is local to one gadget. Then, log into the router’s admin page and check for firmware updates and auto-channel settings, which can improve stability. Finally, if it keeps happening, test with an Ethernet cable; if wired is stable, you may need a new router, less interference, or help from your internet provider.
